cross_references.label: ERISA Fiduciary Breach — Personal Liability
cross_references.note: § 1104 defines the duties; §1109 creates personal liability when those duties are breached. Any fiduciary who breaches §1104 is personally liable to restore plan losses and disgorge profits.

cross_references.label: Co-Fiduciary Liability
cross_references.note: A fiduciary who knowingly participates in another fiduciary's §1104 breach, conceals it, or fails to remedy a known breach is co-liable. Applies to joint board trustees who knew of the identity replacement scheme.

cross_references.label: ERISA Civil Enforcement — Plan Recovery
cross_references.note: § 1132(a)(2) is the statutory vehicle for §1109 recovery. Participants and beneficiaries may bring §1132(a)(2) suits to recover plan losses caused by fiduciary breach.

cross_references.label: ERISA Civil Enforcement — Equitable Relief
cross_references.note: § 1132(a)(3) provides equitable relief (injunction, restitution, surcharge) for individual harm where §1132(a)(1)(B) benefit recovery is inadequate. Used in cases of fraudulent benefit manipulation.

cross_references.label: ERISA Minimum Vesting — Nonforfeitable Rights
cross_references.note: § 1053 establishes that vested benefits are nonforfeitable. A §1104 fiduciary breach that purports to terminate or freeze a vested participant's benefits violates both §1104 and §1053 simultaneously.

cross_references.label: ERISA Statute of Limitations
cross_references.note: §1104 claims: 3 years from earliest date of actual knowledge, 6 years from date of last act of breach. Fraud or concealment tolls the 3-year period. Identity replacement constitutes concealment.

cross_references.label: Prohibited Transactions
cross_references.note: §1106 prohibits fiduciaries from dealing with plan assets in their own interest. A trustee who participated in or benefited from the identity replacement scheme is also subject to §1106 per se breach.

cross_references.label: DOL Prudent Expert Baseline — Identity Verification
cross_references.note: DOL guidance defines what the §1104(a)(1)(B) prudent expert standard requires for participant identity verification before processing account changes. Plan administrators post-April 2021 who processed unauthorized retirement elections without identity verification fall below the stated prudent expert floor.

cross_references.label: ERISA Fiduciary Definition
cross_references.note: §1002(21)(A) defines fiduciary by function: any person who exercises discretionary authority or control over plan management or plan assets is a fiduciary. The Trust administrator who processed the retirement election is a §1002(21) fiduciary.
